params._note: Inputs of dc_sim.arch_study (use case B node-composition study). EVERYTHING here is an ASSUMPTION unless it says FROM quantum_arch / FROM dc_sim assumptions. Use case B numbers follow the Sundai Hack 145 slides (first workload version: Kimi K3-class model); the per-step compute cost uses dc_sim's model_cost_x proxy, NOT the slides' bandwidth step-time model (not imported yet).

pod.note: One site slice. Users are the case-B agent developers served by the pod (all three regions, time-zone mixed). The pod cap is a FACILITY power cap, as in the challenge.

case_b.interactive_note: Slides: interactive tools run on the user's laptop, so they use no data-centre CPU here (orchestration ignored). Background tools run in a sandbox next to the model. Tool time 8 s and 2 cores per step are ASSUMPTIONS (the slides give 8 s only for the laptop case).
case_b.rho_note: Highest accelerator utilisation at which interactive steps still meet their latency target (headroom for bursts); same value as dc_sim's rho_slo.
case_b.bg_wait_note: Background compute may wait this long for spare accelerator capacity (the slides give 4 h per background task; half of it is kept as slack). ASSUMPTION.

cpu.note: TDP 800 W FROM quantum_arch classical.cpu_2035 (about 512 cores). Overhead, idle share, capex, target utilisation, host CPUs per GPU module (one socket per 8 modules, already inside the GPU server overhead) and the share of host-CPU cores free for sandboxes are ASSUMPTIONS.

economics.note: Price: dc_sim's US South site. PUE, facility capex per kW and the GPU capex come from dc_sim's assumptions (liquid cooling; gpu_rack capex per module). Facility capex is charged on PEAK facility power.

quantum.note: QPU power, runtime, acceptance probability and capex-independent feasibility FROM quantum_arch (via dc_sim.qfeas, mid2030s base); capex and calibration windows FROM dc_sim node_types (ASSUMPTION). A call is one quantum-eligible tool call of a background agent. Iterations per call (classical optimiser round trips) and the two link round-trip times are ASSUMPTIONS: a pooled QPU pays iterations x (pool_rtt - local_rtt) extra per call. A call whose predicted wait exceeds max_wait_s is run classically instead (the overflow rule of the scheduler).

grid.note: The two unknowns that decide everything: how many background tasks contain a quantum-eligible call, and what the BEST CLASSICAL method costs for that call at the same accuracy (GPU module-hours). Nobody knows either for agent workloads; the study maps the whole range and reports break-even lines instead of picking a value.

design._note: Inputs of dc_sim.dc_design (architecture v2: pooled GPU nodes, CPU sandbox pool, context-memory pool, shared QPU service, agents PARK their session while a QPU sub-task runs). Shared sections (case_b, cpu, economics, quantum, pod) are read from arch_study.json. EVERYTHING here is an ASSUMPTION unless it says FROM quantum_arch / FROM dc_sim assumptions. The class mix and the quantum-eligible call densities are the scenario, not data: nobody has measured them.

coding_agents.note: case B (slides). Calls: a solver/optimiser tool that happens to be quantum-backed; rare.

mechanical.note: mechanical engineers: optimisation sub-problems (small, classical is cheap)

finance.note: financial engineers: large linear-algebra sub-problems (quantum_arch states no advantage for this kernel)

classical_fallback_module_hours.note: FROM dc_sim assumptions classical_fallback_defaults (ASSUMPTIONS there): cost of the best classical method at the same accuracy.

design.classical_max_note: A call that would cost more than this classically is NOT SERVED by the GPU-only reference (about 64 modules for 3 hours). On a QPU it is served. Unserved calls are valued at this cap in the sizing objective. ASSUMPTION.
design.induced_note: Assumption 1 of the user: with QPUs available, more QPU tasks get created. The call densities above are multiplied by this factor in a scenario; the GPU-only reference faces the same calls (and cannot serve the expensive ones).

parking.note: Park: the session context moves to the context-memory pool; on resume it is copied back (transfer_gbps) or, for recompute_share of the resumes, re-prefilled (cached_ctx_tokens). Hold: the session keeps its KV cache in GPU HBM (ctx_gb of hbm_gb_per_module) for the whole wait + run. Capacity, share and token numbers are ASSUMPTIONS; pool power and capex FROM dc_sim assumptions (ctxmem_pool).

design.classical_cost_scale_note: Multiplies every classical fallback cost; used for sensitivities (the fallback costs are the least certain input).
